item.title: Coworking
item.description: The island has fiber internet along the west coast from Saladan down to Klong Nin. Cafes average around 180 Mbps, and the dedicated coworking spaces hit 1 Gbps. You won’t have connectivity problems here. Coworking spaces # KoHub # KoHub is the biggest coworking space on the island. It’s off the main road near Long Beach, about 10 minutes walk from the sand, with a jungle garden out back. The internet is fast (1 Gbps fiber), there’s good coffee and food on site, and the community is the main draw.

item.title: Food
item.description: Worried about food hygiene? Read our tips on staying healthy while eating out. Breakfast places # Escape Cafe Mem’s Coffee Corner Peak Cafe Bark Tuesday Morning - On weekends. Kohub - Has breakfast too. Restaurants with good fish # Shanti Shanti Beach House - Good fish, win and sunset meals. Best from 6PM-10PM. Laanta Seafood BBQ & American # Joe’s Texas BBQ - Not local or authentically Thai, but a fine Texan surprise at the end of the world.

item.title: Health & Beauty
item.description: Medical # You can walk in to all clinics. Dr. Salarin is a good GP on Long Beach. For something more advanced with testing, Dr. Pad in Saladan is a good option. Thonburi Lanta offers 24-hour emergency care. Dentists # Lanta Dente - Only dentist on the island, on Khlong Dao road. Nails # Cool Nail Studio Barber and haircut # Let me cut Barber - next to Slow Bar Caffetaria.

item.title: Visa
item.description: 93 countries get 60 days visa-free. That’s enough for most visitors. You can extend by 30 days at immigration if you want to stay longer, or apply for a tourist visa (60 days) before your trip. ⚠️ Heads up: Thailand has approved cutting visa-free stays from 60 to 30 days for most nationalities (and fewer eligible countries). It’s not in effect yet as of mid-2026, but it could take effect at short notice — always check the current rule before you book.

item.title: Accommodation
item.description: Most nomads stay around Long Beach (Phra Ae) since it’s close to KoHub. Prices vary a lot by season. High season (Dec-Feb) books up fast and costs roughly double what you’d pay in shoulder months (Nov, Mar-Apr). If you’re coming in peak season, book ahead. Outside of that, you can often just show up and walk around. Some places are cheaper when you message them directly on WhatsApp or Facebook. Monthly rates are almost always negotiable in person.

item.title: Drinks
item.description: Craft Beer # Devy Ale Cafe - Best craft beer selection on the island. Located at the end of Saladan road. Great selection of Thai craft beers (brewed in Cambodia/Laos due to Thai laws). Expect 230-240 baht per beer. Bonnies Deli - Shop that sells a good selection of craft beers. Wine # Seven Seas at Pimalai Resort - Fine dining with extensive wine list. Cocktails # Sugggestions welcome! Nice bars # Pangea Beach Bar - Long Beach.

item.title: Trips & Activities
item.description: Cooking Classes # Time for Lime # The original Thai cooking school on Koh Lanta, open since 2002. Located on Klong Dao Beach in an open-air beachfront setting with a pool. Classes run ~5.5 hours — you make curry paste, 2 starters, and 2 main courses, then eat what you cooked. A cocktail class is included in some packages. Recipes are sent home with you. A portion of all profits goes to Lanta Animal Welfare, which rescues and treats stray animals on the island.

item.title: Parties
item.description: There is a more or less fixed schedule for the parties on the island. The big ones have a fixed day of the week. Some bars are a bit hidden but when they are the main party that night there will be torches outside on the main road to guide you there. Monday # Pub Quiz at the Irish Embassy Irie Bar - Live music Tuesday # Pangea, starts at 21:00.

item.title: Sports
item.description: Gyms # WM Fitness - Long Beach area. Modern gym with good selection of cardio equipment, resistance machines, and free weights. Also has a rig area with battle ropes, sandbags, kettlebells. Connected to William Muay Thai Stadium. Air conditioned. Day pass 200 THB. See Facebook for full pricing information. Luke’s Gym - European style gym in Klong Khong, surrounded by jungle. Dumbbells up to 50kg, many machines. Very clean with separate changing rooms and showers.

item.title: Transportation
item.description: There’s no public transport on Koh Lanta. Most people rent a scooter and that’s pretty much all you need. The island is about 30km from north to south, so even the longest trip only takes around 40 minutes. Getting to the island # Most people fly into Krabi Airport and then take a transfer to Koh Lanta. The drive takes about 2 to 2.5 hours depending on traffic and ferry wait times.

item.title: Money
item.description: Cash is king on Koh Lanta. Most local restaurants, massage shops, markets and small businesses only accept cash. Bigger restaurants, hotels and convenience stores like 7-Eleven take Visa and Mastercard, but don’t count on it everywhere. Always have cash on hand. Photo by Q L on Pexels (free to use) ATMs # ATMs are scattered across the island, mostly at 7-Elevens and bank branches. You’ll find them in Saladan, Klong Dao, Long Beach and Klong Nin.

item.title: Getting to Koh Lanta
item.description: Most people fly into Krabi and take a road transfer. From Bangkok, count on 5-6 hours door to door: the flight itself is short, but the transfer and ferry crossing eat up the rest. Fly to Krabi, then drive # Krabi Airport is the closest airport. Direct flights from Bangkok take about 1.5 hours. Thai Airways and Bangkok Airways fly from Suvarnabhumi (BKK). Budget airlines like AirAsia, Nok Air, and Thai Lion Air fly from Don Mueang (DMK).

item.title: Is there Grab on Koh Lanta?
item.description: No. Grab doesn’t work on Koh Lanta, and neither does Bolt or any other ride-hailing app. The island is too small and too far from the mainland for any of them to operate here. If you’re coming from Bangkok, Chiang Mai, or even Krabi town, you’re used to opening an app and having a car show up. That won’t happen here. Put the phone away and read on. How people actually get around # Most people rent a scooter.
